title: Add response caching + single-flight coalescing for cacheable GET routes
description:
Not yet in docs/plan/plan.md — a new improvement idea grounded in SEAM's actual topology: it will be
the single chokepoint for dozens of concurrent NEEDLE workers hitting the same read-only upstreams
(ArgoCD app list, per-cluster kubectl-proxy `get pods`, etc.). Right now every fragment's requests
pass straight through with no caching, so N workers polling the same status at the same moment means
N upstream calls.

Proposed addition: a route fragment extension `x-cache-ttl` (seconds) marking a route's response as
safe to cache; the gateway serves repeat identical requests (same route + normalized params) from an
in-memory cache within the TTL, and single-flights concurrent identical in-flight requests (only one
upstream call in-flight per (route, params) key, all concurrent callers await the same result) even
for TTL=0 (dedup only, no caching).

This is a genuine efficiency win specific to SEAM's fleet-of-callers shape, not generic advice.
Write it up as a new subsection in docs/plan/plan.md (pattern-match the existing "Per-Route Guards"
section: opt-in per route via fragment field, no SEAM-wide default) and add it as a phase or fold
into an existing one (natural fit: extends Phase 1's request-handling core). Should note the
interaction with the Credential Health Sentinel's probe traffic and with cost-governed routes
(x-cost-per-call) — a cache hit should not count against x-quota.

title: 2.1: OpenBao client + 30s cache + outage behavior
description: Phase 2 (Architecture -> OpenBao auth; secret caching; secret-store outage behavior, decided 2026-07-22). Kubernetes auth in-cluster; dev-token mode locally (env/flag, REFUSED when in-cluster detected via projected SA token or KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST, enumerated at /config/status as authMode: dev-token); 30 s in-memory cache keyed by resolved x-vault-path; eager 401 invalidation. title: 12.2: 401 refetch-retry-once + credential-refresh-not-retried
description: Phase 12 (Credential Health Sentinel; Scenario 4). On an upstream 401: eagerly invalidate the cached secret, refetch from OpenBao, RE-STRIP inbound headers, re-inject the fresh value, retry exactly ONCE over the Phase 2 tee (body within maxReplayableRequestBytes) - the caller sees a transparent success and /health/credentials reflects the refresh. Above the cap or unreplayable: still invalidate + refetch (next request succeeds), do NOT retry, answer with the structured credential-refresh-not-retried envelope (upstream's own status, scrubbed body, plain statement that resending now uses the refreshed credential). If the refetch itself fails, degrade to the secret-store-unavailable 503 (2.1). Charged twice on the retry path per the dispatch-time accounting rule. Scenario 4 green in both forms.

title: Implement single-flight request coalescing
description:
## Overview

Implement single-flight coalescing to deduplicate concurrent identical in-flight requests.

## Scope

- Track in-flight requests by (route, params) key
- When multiple concurrent identical requests arrive, await the same in-flight call
- Only one upstream call per key at a time
- Support TTL=0 mode (dedup only, no caching)
- Integrate with cache layer (single-flight both cache misses and TTL=0)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In-flight request tracking implemented
- [ ] Concurrent identical requests coalesce to single upstream call
- [ ] All waiters receive the same response
- [ ] TTL=0 dedup mode works
- [ ] Works with cache layer (cache misses are single-flighted)
- [ ] Thread-safe concurrent access
notes:
Verified implementation is complete:

✅ In-flight request tracking: SingleFlight.inFlight map[CacheKey]*inFlightRequest tracks all in-flight requests by (route, params) key

✅ Concurrent identical requests coalesce: Do() method checks if request already in-flight, waiters call waitForResult() instead of making new upstream call

✅ All waiters receive same response: inFlightRequest stores result/err, all waiters receive these via waitForResult() returning req.result/req.err

✅ TTL=0 dedup mode works: cache_middleware.go:94 checks 'if ttl > 0' for caching, but single-flight is applied at line 40 BEFORE this, so TTL=0 still gets deduped

✅ Works with cache layer: cacheMiddleware() uses s.singleFlight.Do() wrapping executeAndCacheRequest(), ensuring cache misses are single-flighted

✅ Thread-safe: Uses sync.Mutex protecting inFlight map, atomic operations for metrics counters

Comprehensive tests confirm:
- TestSingleFlight_Coalescing: 10 concurrent requests → 1 execution
- TestSingleFlight_TTLZeroDedup: TTL=0 sequential requests call upstream each time (no cache)
- TestSingleFlight_ConcurrentTTLZero: 5 concurrent TTL=0 requests → 1 execution (deduped)
- TestSingleFlight_ContextCancellation: Context cleanup works correctly
- TestSingleFlight_MultipleKeys: Different keys handled independently

All tests pass successfully. Implementation complete and working.

4. TTL=0 dedup works (single-flight applied before caching check)

title: 12.1: Sentinel probe loop + Lease + /health/credentials + exclusions
description: Phase 12 (Credential Health Sentinel). Background loop issuing each fragment's x-credential-probe (per-fragment cadence, per-entry probeInterval override) as a byte-identical authenticated request carrying an IN-PROCESS origin tag (never a wire header - all X-SEAM-* are stripped on ingress, so the tag is unforgeable). Lease-elected: acquire the Kubernetes Lease before probing, drop on SIGTERM; without the Lease serve traffic but probe NOTHING (fail closed; consumes the 6a Role/RoleBinding, adds no RBAC). /health/credentials per (fragment, instance) (_default for single-instance): lastVerified, status, known expiry, per-instance probe-spend rate - never values. Exclusions per consumer: OUT of the retirement counter, loop breaker, and quota; IN last-2xx and breaker state with source: probe labeling. Deprecated fragments keep probing; adapting fragments never probe; probe on a pass-through is a lint error.

title: 11.1: Per-origin circuit breaker + x-breaker + structured 503
description: Phase 11 (Passive Route Health owns the policy). Failure = transport faults (refused/reset, DNS, TLS handshake), timeouts, and 5xx ONLY - no 4xx ever counts, and a 401 NEVER counts (even one triggering refetch-retry); SEAM's own 400/429/500 never count. 5 consecutive -> open 30 s; half-open admits ONE real caller (no synthetic probe), any non-failure closes, re-failure re-opens with backoff 30/60/120 s capped at 5 min; keyed on resolved upstream origin (scheme+host+port; per x-upstream-map entry). Structured 503: upstream, openedAt, lastError, derived Retry-After (seconds remaining, floored at 1, body matches header). x-breaker {threshold, openSeconds, maxOpenSeconds, enabled} fragment-root + per-instance override; same-origin disagreement: lint fails the PR, runtime strictest values govern with the disagreement at /config/status; ON BY DEFAULT - enabled: false is the lint-flagged, enumerated opt-out.
